item.title: Hours in line, barely enough gas for one trip
item.description:
CNG driver Abdul Alim arrived at a filling station in Mohakhali at 6:30am to refuel. After waiting for around two and a half hours, he received just Tk42 worth of gas. With that, he made his first trip of the day, carrying a passenger to Banasree for Tk300.
After dropping off the passenger, Alim waited at the CNG stand on FG Avenue for his next fare, where he spoke about the ordeal.
“What am I supposed to do with Tk42 worth of gas after waiting for two and a half hours?” Alim said. “I’ve completed one trip and may be able to make one more. Then I’ll have to find a filling station and queue up for gas again. After waiting for hours, I may get another Tk50 or Tk60 worth of gas. Maybe I’ll be able to make two more trips. At this rate, the whole day will be over.”
The daily rental for his CNG is Tk1,200.
“I won’t even be able to cover the rental. What will I eat? What will my family eat?” he said.
Alim is not alone. CNG drivers across the capital are facing the same situation, spending most of the day waiting for gas and struggling to earn enough to cover their daily rentals.
Private car driver Yunus said he too was waiting for hours to get only Tk100-Tk120 worth of gas.
“My 1,500cc car can take gas worth Tk600. How far can I go with Tk120 worth of gas?” he said.
Yunus said he operates a rent-a-car under a monthly contract of Tk30,000.
“How am I supposed to operate with Tk120 worth of gas? Most of my fares are outside Dhaka. And how far can I travel outside Dhaka with Tk120 worth of gas?” he said.
“I can’t even cross Kanchpur amid this gas crisis. So how will I pay the contract amount and run my household?” he added.
Visiting several sites has shown that the crisis has shown no sign of improvement. Since Tuesday morning, severe shortages have been reported at CNG filling stations as well as in households across the capital.
The acute gas shortage has caused widespread distress in Dhaka and elsewhere in the country. CNG-powered transport operators are among the worst affected, with drivers spending much of their working day waiting in queues at filling stations. Even after waiting for hours, the amount of gas they receive is often insufficient for more than one or two trips.
Several CNG stations have also been forced to shut down because of low gas pressure.
Long queues of vehicles were seen at CNG stations in Gabtoli, Kallyanpur, Kalshi, Kazipara and Shewrapara. With gas supplies reduced, private cars, microbuses and auto-rickshaws were forced to wait for long periods to refuel.
The situation was similar in Demra, where transport workers had to wait more than two to three hours for gas at CNG filling stations. Long lines of vehicles formed outside the stations.
Unable to take passengers regularly, many drivers are struggling to earn a living and support their families. Meanwhile, filling station owners are also incurring losses as gas sales decline.
Mohammad Bashir Howlader, a rent-a-car driver at Russell Filling and CNG Station, said, “We are suffering losses every day because we are not getting enough gas. We cannot take long-distance passengers. It is no longer possible to take passengers and then stop to refuel because we have to remain in line for hours. If this continues, our entire families will have to starve.”
The gas shortage was more severe than usual in Mugda, Maniknagar, Sabujbagh, Khilgaon, Banasree and Hajipara, where gas pressure was reportedly at its lowest.
The shortage caused severe difficulties for CNG-powered vehicle drivers, while several filling stations were seen displaying signs saying they had no gas.
The gas crisis was particularly severe in Uttara. Most CNG filling stations had suspended supplies due to a lack of gas. At stations that remained operational, long queues of vehicles formed because of low gas pressure.
Kamal Ahmed, manager of Khandakar Filling Station, said: “A large portion of the transport sector depends on gas. So when gas pressure is low, long queues of vehicles form. There is nothing we can do to solve these problems.”

item.title: Tribunal sends four, including Badi-Miftah, to jail in Ekram murder case
item.description:
The International Crimes Tribunal has ordered four accused, including former Cox’s Bazar-4 MP Abdur Rahman Badi, to be sent to jail in a crimes against humanity case over the alleged killing of Teknaf councillor Ekramul Haque in a staged gunfight in Cox’s Bazar.
The tribunal also ordered newspaper notices seeking the surrender of seven other accused, including ousted former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, who are absconding in the case.
The other three accused sent to jail are Brigadier General Miftah Uddin Ahmed, Brigadier General Mahbub Alam and former RAB director general Anwar Latif Khan. All four were produced before the tribunal on Tuesday. Mahbub and Anwar are already detained at the Dhaka Cantonment sub-jail in connection with another case.
A single-member bench of International Crimes Tribunal-2, headed by Judge Md Manjurul Bashid, passed the order following a prosecution petition.
Apart from Sheikh Hasina, the other absconding accused are former home minister Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal, former bridges minister Obaidul Quader, former inspector general of police Benazir Ahmed, Major (retd) Ruhul Amin, Lieutenant Commander Ashequr Rahman and former DGFI officer Squadron Leader Nazmus Shakib Mahmud.
Prosecutor Dr Mohammad Oli Mia appeared for the prosecution, accompanied by prosecutors Faruk Ahmed, Moinul Karim, Marjina Raihan and others.
During the hearing, Oli told the tribunal that it had taken formal charges against 11 people, including Sheikh Hasina, into cognizance on July 26. The tribunal also issued production warrants against three accused and arrest warrants against seven.
Four accused were produced before the tribunal on Tuesday, while the whereabouts of the remaining seven could not be established despite searches at their permanent and temporary addresses. Non-execution reports (NERs) were subsequently submitted to the tribunal.
The prosecution then sought orders to send the four accused to jail in connection with the case and publish newspaper notices asking the remaining seven to surrender.
After the hearing, the tribunal approved the prosecution's petitions, ordered the four accused to be sent to jail and set September 7 for the next hearing.
According to the prosecution, Ekramul Haque was picked up from a road in front of Hotel Netong in Kerantoli, Teknaf, Cox’s Bazar, at around 10:30pm on May 26, 2018.
He was allegedly killed in a staged gunfight with RAB personnel between 11pm and midnight on Marine Drive in Noakhalia Para, Teknaf Sadar Union.
Ekramul was a councillor of Ward No. 3 of Teknaf municipality and president of the upazila unit of Jubo League.
The prosecution has brought charges against the accused of illegal detention, abduction, shooting and killing through a staged gunfight, involvement in and instigation of crimes, aiding and abetting, and ordering the killing.

item.description:
The government will hold discussions with the Election Commission next week to learn about its preparations for the upcoming local government elections, said State Minister for Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives Mir Shahe Alam on Tuesday.
Talking to reporters at the secretariat, he said he would visit the Election Commission with the prime minister’s approval to discuss the state of its preparations.
“We may go to the Election Commission next week, with the honorable prime minister’s approval, and discuss how far their preparations have progressed and what the situation is,” he said.
The state minister said the Election Commission would announce the election schedule and conduct the polls, while the government would provide necessary support as the local government institutions fall under his ministry.
“The Election Commission will announce the schedule. It will conduct the elections and bring the election results from the field,” he said.
He said the ministry would provide support regarding election expenses and other related matters, including the expiration of the terms of the local government institutions.
Asked whether he had any information about the election schedule, Mir Shahe Alam said the Election Commission itself would be able to provide details.
Asked whether the government had made any proposal regarding the elections, he said the government had already allocated funds for holding five local government elections in the current fiscal year.
“As I have said many times before, we have kept Tk6,000 crore in the current fiscal year’s budget required to hold these five elections,” he said.

Hog Plum farmers log better business in Rangamati
item.description:
Hog plum is now in season across the hills of Rangamati, with trees laden with the popular sweet-and-sour fruit in homesteads, orchards and along roadsides.
For many Indigenous and Bengali communities, hog plum is more than a seasonal fruit. It has become an important source of income, particularly for women who collect the fruit and sell it in local markets.
The reddish soil and humid climate of Rangamati are considered suitable for hog plum cultivation. Local varieties are mainly grown in the district and require relatively little care. The trees can grow naturally around homes, along roads and on fallow land.
The fruiting season generally peaks during the Bengali months of Bhadra and Ashwin. Hog plum is green when unripe and turns light yellow as it matures.
The fruit is widely consumed across the district. Many people eat raw hog plum with salt and chilli, while ripe fruit is used to make pickles, chutney, juice and preserves.
Hog plum is currently being sold at Reserve Bazar and Banarupa Bazar in Rangamati town, as well as in markets across different upazilas. Retail prices currently range between Tk60 and Tk80 per kilogram.
Indigenous women vendors are bringing hog plum to town in baskets and selling it, helping supplement their household incomes.
Janki Rakhine, a hog plum vendor, said sales remain good during the season.
“Hoc plum sells well during the season. If government support and market access are increased, women in the hills will benefit even more,” she said.
Another vendor, Md Selim, said demand for the fruit is strong in local markets.
“Many customers buy both raw and ripe hog plum every day,” he said.
According to the Rangamati Agriculture Department, hog plum is cultivated on around 24 hectares of land in the district, with annual production estimated at approximately 240 tonnes. The potential market value of the production is around Tk60 lakh.
Rangamati Agriculture Officer Md Moniruzzaman said the agriculture department is assisting farmers by providing improved varieties of seedlings and necessary agricultural advice.
He also stressed the need for fruit-processing facilities to increase the value of locally produced fruits.
“Fruit-processing industries are necessary for value addition to all types of fruit. If processing factories are established in Rangamati, the district’s hog plum could eventually be exported beyond the country,” he said.
However, despite good production, a considerable amount of hog plum is wasted every year due to inadequate marketing and storage facilities.
Agricultural stakeholders say the establishment of cold-storage facilities and modern fruit-processing plants could reduce post-harvest losses and create new economic opportunities for hill communities.
With improved storage, market access and value-added processing, Rangamati’s hog plum has the potential to become an important contributor to the district’s rural economy while opening up opportunities for wider domestic and international markets.

item.title: Upstream water floods homes, croplands in Brahmanbaria
item.description:
A sudden surge of water from India’s Tripura state inundated low-lying areas of at least 15 villages in Akhaura upazila of Brahmanbaria on Monday, submerging croplands, fish farms and vegetable fields and forcing several families to leave their homes.
Residents said water began rushing into the area in the early hours of the day through the Haora River and the Jaji and Kalandi canals following heavy rainfall in the hilly areas of Tripura.
The flooding has affected low-lying areas of Dakshin Union, including Anwarpur, Hirapur, Abdullahpur, Dhaleshwar, Banger Char, Bautla, Birchandrapur, Sahebnagar and Umedpur. Several areas of Akhaura municipality, including Narayanpur, Taragaon and Dhatur Pahila, have also been inundated.
Low-lying areas of Mogra Union’s Colonel Bazar and parts of Moniand Union have also been affected.
Water has entered homes and business establishments around the Akhaura Land Port, disrupting the activities of small traders. Residents of some inundated homes have moved to relatives’ houses for shelter.
Farmers said they were particularly concerned about damage to their crops.
“After spending a lot of money and effort to cultivate paddy, I have now lost the entire crop to the floodwater,” said Abdur Rashid, a farmer from Abdullahpur. “If the water recedes, I do not know how I will cultivate the land again. The government should provide compensation to affected farmers.”
Monu Mia, another farmer from Birchandrapur, said his paddy fields were underwater and warned that continued rises in the water level could cause major losses.
Tajul Islam, a farmer from Rajendrapur, said around four kani of his paddy land had been submerged. He said the crop might still be saved if the water receded quickly, but prolonged flooding would cause significant damage.
Mahbub Mia, a small trader near the Akhaura Land Port, said water entered several shops and business establishments early yesterday.
“If the water continues to rise, the suffering of local residents will increase,” he said.
Abdur Rahim Mia, a member of Ward No. 8 of Dakshin Union, said heavy rainfall in the hilly areas of Tripura had caused the sudden surge of water, which entered Akhaura through the Haora River and the Jaji and Kalandi canals.
Several families have already been affected and taken shelter with relatives, he said.
Akhaura Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) Tapasi Rabeya said the administration had assessed the initial damage caused by the influx of water from upstream.
“Thirty-two families have so far been affected, while around 1,400 hectares of cropland are underwater,” she said.
She said the administration was monitoring the situation and had kept local primary schools ready to be used as emergency shelters if the water level rose further.
Dry food, rice, relief materials and medicines have also been kept ready, she said.
However, officials said the situation had started to improve somewhat from the afternoon as the water level began to recede.
Local residents and officials said further heavy rainfall in Tripura could worsen the situation, while a continued decline in the water level could help limit the damage.

item.title: MAF urges Cyber Security Act changes to curb online abuse
item.description:
The Multiparty Advocacy Forum (MAF) has called for amendments to the Cyber Security Act, 2026, to introduce clear legal protection against technology-facilitated gender-based violence (TFGBV), saying the law does not adequately address online abuse.
The forum made the demand at a press conference at the Tofazzal Hossain Manik Mia Hall of the National Press Club, where it presented a six-point set of recommendations for a safe, inclusive and accountable digital environment.
Speakers said TFGBV should be recognized as a distinct and serious offence under the law. They said the Cyber Security Act, 2026, lacks clear definitions of TFGBV and “consent” and does not specifically address emerging forms of digital violence, including deepfakes, sextortion, cyberflashing, cyberstalking, doxxing and coordinated online harassment.
Speakers said TFGBV was not merely a cybercrime but a serious threat to human rights, personal safety and the equal participation of women and marginalized communities.
They urged policymakers to adopt the recommendations and make the Cyber Security Act more effective, victim-centered and responsive to emerging forms of digital abuse. They also called for active media cooperation to raise public awareness about TFGBV.
Members of Parliament Nadia Pathan Papon and Sultana Jasmine Jui spoke on the need to include TFGBV in the law and ensure legal protection for victims.
The written statement was presented by Sayra Chandra Chakma, joint general secretary of the central committee of Chhatra Dal, and Golam Mostafa, joint convener of the Bangladesh Youth Federation. The programme was moderated by Enzamul Haque of the NCP and Nasrin Rahman Popi of Chhatra Dal.
MAF Vice-President and Dhaka South BNP Joint Convener Saidur Rahman Mintu, MAF member and central Mohila Dal office secretary Shahinur Nargis, and leaders of various political parties also spoke.
The press conference was held under the B-SPACE project, implemented by Democracy International and funded by the United Kingdom’s Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO).

item.title: Draft NHRC law faces criticism over government control
item.description:
The draft National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) Act, 2026 has come under sharp criticism from civil society leaders, legal experts and human rights activists, who say government-dominated appointment procedures and prior approval requirements could undermine the commission’s independence.
The proposed law, while containing some positive revisions, also has internal contradictions and provisions that could restrict the commission’s ability to investigate rights violations independently, speakers said at a consultation in Dhaka on Monday.
The meeting, titled “Draft National Human Rights Commission Act, 2026: Review and Recommendations,” was organized by the Bangladesh Legal Aid and Services Trust (BLAST) at Tofazzal Hossain Manik Miah Hall of the National Press Club.
Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB) Executive Director Dr Iftekharuzzaman questioned whether the proposed selection process would produce a genuinely independent commission.
“Of the nine members of the selection committee, all except two remain under government control. Under such a structure, expecting an independent and neutral human rights commission is unrealistic,” he said.
He also criticized a provision requiring government approval to establish NHRC regional offices outside Dhaka, saying it could further undermine the commission’s institutional autonomy.
“We hope policymakers will reconsider these issues,” he said.
Nagorik Uddyog Chief Executive Zakir Hossain questioned why a body described as independent would require prior government approval to perform its functions.
“If an independent commission truly means independent, why should prior approval be necessary? Merely labelling it an independent commission does not make it one,” he said.
He also proposed that the commission’s budgetary allocations be made directly on the basis of its recommendations rather than through separate and potentially redundant funding mechanisms.
Human rights activist and former NHRC member Nur Khan Liton raised concerns over provisions requiring prior authorization for on-the-spot inspections.
“An investigation that requires prior permission holds no real value,” he said, pointing to what he described as contradictions in several provisions of the draft.
“We need a robust legal framework, but we also need to constitute a commission with honest and courageous individuals,” Liton added.
Supreme Court advocate Dr Kazi Zahed Iqbal highlighted potential legal complications involving evidence and compensation.
“There are critical questions regarding the evidentiary status of reports submitted by the commission in serious or criminal cases,” he said.
He also warned that the process of enforcing compensation could become caught up in bureaucratic delays and called for a separate, streamlined mechanism.
Sara Hossain, honorary executive director of BLAST and a senior Supreme Court advocate, called for a thorough parliamentary review of the proposed legislation.
“We want a well-thought-out Human Rights Commission Act. Section 19 has drawn significant debate given our lived experiences over the past two years,” she said.
She stressed that the commission must be capable of protecting the rights of all citizens, particularly marginalized communities, persons with disabilities and indigenous peoples.
Sara said BLAST would prepare specific recommendations and submit them to the Ministry of Law, while also making them available to the public.
Other participants called for reforms to make the commission more accessible and responsive to citizens.
Shireen Parveen Huq, founder member of Naripokkho and chair of the Women Affairs Reform Commission; Barrister Khan Khalid Adnan, a Supreme Court advocate; Satej Chakma, international affairs secretary of the Bangladesh Adivasi Youth Forum; author and researcher Anupam Debashis Roy; and Bhaskar Bhattacharjee, inclusion adviser at YPSA, took part in the discussion.
They called for digital complaint mechanisms and simpler administrative and management procedures so that people in rural areas, indigenous communities and persons with disabilities can access the commission’s services more easily.
Speakers said ensuring institutional independence, transparent appointment procedures and accessible complaint and investigation mechanisms would be crucial for the NHRC to function as an effective rights-protection body.

item.title: Study: Coastal salinity puts one in five at heart disease risk
item.description:
More than half of the drinking water sources in Khulna’s coastal upazila of Koyra have high salinity levels, while one in five adults aged 40 and above in Koyra and Satkhira’s Ashashuni face moderate to high risk of developing cardiovascular disease within the next decade, according to preliminary findings of a joint study.
The findings were presented on Sunday at a policy seminar titled “Drinking Water Salinity and Health in Bangladesh: Evidence, Adaptation and Policy Solutions” at icddr,b’s Sasakawa Auditorium in Mohakhali.
The study was conducted by icddr,b in collaboration with Imperial College London.
Researchers surveyed 27,697 water sources across 172 villages under 71 community clinics in Koyra and Ashashuni. Of these, 6,703 sources were used for drinking water.
The study found salinity in 55.3% of drinking water sources in Koyra, compared with 23.3% in Ashashuni.
Based on the findings, researchers proposed an integrated intervention package combining access to safe drinking water with primary healthcare.
The plan includes expanding access to low-salinity drinking water through community rainwater harvesting systems, pond sand filters and tube wells, alongside digital registries and routine monitoring of water sources.
The initiative also aims to strengthen the screening and treatment of hypertension, diabetes and chronic kidney disease through primary healthcare, supported by an algorithm-based clinical decision support system for screening, referral, treatment and follow-up.
Imperial College London Professor Adrian Butler said storm surges caused by tropical cyclones can lead to long-term salinization of ponds and shallow groundwater.
He stressed the need to restore water sources quickly after cyclones and maintain coastal polders and embankments.
icddr,b Executive Director Dr Tahmeed Ahmed said Bangladesh still has limited evidence on the links between climate change and health.
He said effective adaptation requires integrating safe drinking water, primary healthcare and community participation.
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change Secretary In-Charge Fahmida Khanom said drinking water salinity is both a climate adaptation and public health challenge that requires coordinated efforts across the environment, health, water and local government sectors.
Dr Md Lutfor Rahman, director general of the Department of Environment, said research of this kind provides institutions responsible for environmental management with a stronger basis for policy action.
“We need to strengthen monitoring and generate data for evidence-based decisions on managing drinking water in salinity-affected areas,” he said.
Director General of the Directorate General of Health Services Professor Dr Pravath Chandra Biswas said there was already years of evidence on the links between salinity and health.
“The task is to bring that evidence together and translate it into practical guidance and policy, while strengthening prevention and management of non-communicable diseases through primary healthcare,” he said.
The seminar also highlighted the need for stronger water quality monitoring, health-based sodium guidelines for drinking water, greater inter-ministerial coordination and sustainable management of drinking water sources.

item.title: 3 held over murder of Gazipur auto-rickshaw driver
item.description:
The Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) has arrested three people in connection with the killing of a 60-year-old auto-rickshaw driver in Kapasia, Gazipur, allegedly to steal his battery-powered vehicle. The victim’s 75-year-old mother also died of cardiac arrest after learning about her son’s death.
The deceased, Ataur Rahman alias Ata Mia, was killed on Thursday near Mirzanagar Girls’ High School in Dakkhin Gaogaan under Sonmania union. He had left home around 4pm with his auto-rickshaw, worth about Tk1.4 lakh, to earn a living. The attackers allegedly strangled him with a rope and struck him with an iron rod and hammer before fleeing with the vehicle and his mobile phone.
According to Gazipur PBI Superintendent of Police Md Rakibul Akter, Ataur left home around 4pm on Thursday with his auto-rickshaw, worth around Tk1.4 lakh, to earn a living.
The arrested suspects are Rajib Khan, Nakibul Hasan Rakib, both from Kapasia, and Mohammad Kibria, owner of Al-Madina Enterprise at Hatirdia bus stand in Narsingdi’s Monohardi.
A case was filed with Kapasia Police Station on Friday. The PBI later took over the investigation and arrested Rajib and Rakib within 24 hours using digital forensic analysis and confidential information.
Following their information, investigators recovered the stolen auto-rickshaw from Al-Madina Enterprise and arrested Kibria for allegedly purchasing and keeping the stolen vehicle. The PBI also recovered Tk22,000 from its sale and the weapons and rope allegedly used in the killing. The suspects reportedly sold the vehicle for Tk42,000 and shared the money.
According to the PBI, Rajib and Rakib confessed under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, saying they planned the robbery because of debt and targeted Ataur because Rakib was distantly related to him.

item.title: Kurigram farmers break into dealer’s warehouse, take away 197 sacks of fertilizer
item.description:
Farmers broke into a fertiliser dealer’s warehouse and took away 197 sacks of urea and MOP fertiliser in Kurigram’s Bhurungamari upazila on Sunday, alleging an artificial shortage and overcharging.
The incident occurred around noon at Dhaldanga Bazar in Shilkhuri Union.
Police and local BNP leaders were present at the scene when the farmers broke through the warehouse’s tin fencing and took the fertiliser.
Additional police later arrived and brought the situation under control. By the afternoon, 58 of the 197 sacks had been returned, while most of the fertiliser remained unaccounted for.
According to locals, preparations were underway to distribute fertiliser at M/s Shah Amanat Enterprise, a BCIC-authorised dealer in the union. Four police personnel and local BNP leaders were present during the distribution.
Several farmers alleged that they had been visiting the dealer for days but were unable to obtain fertiliser. They claimed the dealer was selling part of the union’s allocated supply to retail traders, leaving farmers unable to buy enough fertiliser.
They also alleged that a sack priced at Tk1,300 was being sold by traders for Tk1,800–1,900, causing losses to farmers and threatening their crops.
Taifur Rahman Mukul, proprietor of M/s Shah Amanat Enterprise, said preparations were underway to distribute fertiliser when several people surrounded him and broke through the warehouse fencing.
“Farmers took away 197 sacks of urea and MOP fertiliser. The situation became so tense that police and the administration struggled to control it,” he said, adding that he would file a case over the incident.
Upazila Agriculture Officer Abdul Jabbar, however, denied allegations of a fertiliser shortage or sales above the government-fixed price.
“There is no fertiliser shortage in the union where the incident occurred. We are trying to recover the fertiliser,” he said.
However, a mobile court led by Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) Amrit Deb Nath later found evidence supporting the farmers’ allegation that fertiliser was being sold to retail traders instead of farmers.
The mobile court fined a dealer Tk5,000 in Paglahat area of Shilkhuri Union over the allegation.
“We are conducting inspections at dealer points and retail markets, taking the farmers’ complaints seriously,” the UNO said.
Bhurungamari Police Station Officer-in-Charge Azim Uddin told the Dhaka Tribune that 197 sacks of fertiliser were taken away during the distribution.
“Fearing they would not get fertiliser, people who had come to collect it took away the sacks,” he said.
Police had recovered 58 sacks by the afternoon, he said, adding that legal action would be taken if the remaining fertiliser was not returned.

item.title: Rangpur Police, bKash hold workshop to prevent online gambling, fraud, and criminal activities
item.description:
As part of ongoing efforts to make Mobile Financial Services (MFS) more secure while preventing their misuse in online gambling, fraud, and other criminal activities, a workshop titled “Investigation and Prevention of Misuse of Mobile Financial Services” was held in Rangpur.
A total of 45 investigating officers of the district police attended this daylong workshop, organized by Rangpur district police and bKash, at the police lines hall room.
The workshop sheds light on how law enforcement can leverage transactional data to identify criminal gangs and bring them to justice.
To date, 4,500 officials from various law enforcement bodies have benefited from these sessions held across the country.
Mohammad Mozammel Haque, Superintendent of Police, Rangpur, attended the workshop as chief guest.
On behalf of bKash, EVP and head of external affairs Major AKM Monirul Karim (retd) was present at the workshop.
The workshops featured detailed discussions on leveraging technology to track customers’ lost funds, preventing offences such as online gambling, fraud, and kidnapping through digital transaction monitoring, and establishing swift communication channels between investigating officers and bKash officials.
In particular, the session highlighted how MFS transaction data can be utilized to trace financial trails and apprehend individuals or syndicates involved in online gambling and other cybercrimes.
Additionally, the session emphasized immediate protocols to follow when a criminal incident occurs.
Notably, every transaction can be monitored and tracked as each digital transaction leaves a footprint.
This allows investigative bodies, including the Police, DB, CID, and PBI, to carry out the investigation process more accurately. In this regard, bKash has been continuously organizing workshops titled “Investigation and Prevention of Mobile Financial Services Misuse” with different stakeholders since 2017.

item.title: Toffee extends World Cup success into new EPL season
item.description:
Toffee will be carrying forward its record-breaking Fifa World Cup 2026 streaming success by live streaming the 2026-27 English Premier League Season (EPL).
All league matches can be streamed live by Toffee subscribers in Full HD.
Football fans have been eagerly waiting to watch their favorite players back on the pitch following the world cup season.
The wait comes to an end with the beginning of the 35th season of English Premier League where fans will find their favorite players back in action.
Building on this momentum, Toffee is now bringing the full 2026-27 English Premier League (EPL) season to viewers, with matches taking place across 38 weeks.

On the other hand, Toffee is also offering the short EPL Pass for Tk99 for 30 days, through which Toffee subscribers will also be able to live stream the matches in full HD and this pack will also be supported in three devices.
Toffee subscribers will also be able to watch other football tournaments such as UEFA Champions Legue, Bundesliga and The FA Cup through the platform’s international TV channels and all these matches can be viewed live.
The viewers will need to keep an eye on the Toffee app to be notified about all the upcoming contents.
Commenting on the initiative, Modasser Ahmed, head of Toffee, Banglalink, said: “The Fifa World Cup 2026 was a defining moment for Toffee, with millions of football fans choosing our platform to experience the biggest tournament in the world. We are excited to build on this momentum as we bring another season of the Premier League to Toffee viewers across Bangladesh. With a strong focus on delivering a seamless and engaging viewing experience, we look forward to making this EPL season another memorable one for Toffee users.”
Subscribers can sign up through the Toffee app or website to avail themselves of their preferred EPL pass.

item.title: Swapon calls for expanding tree plantation social movement
item.description:
The prime minister's political adviser, Zahir Uddin Swapon, on Sunday called for expanding the ongoing social movement for tree plantation and greening.
He made the call at a discussion organized by the Krishibid Association as part of a tree plantation program at the Bangladesh Agricultural Research Institute auditorium in Gazipur.
Zahir Uddin Swapon said, “It is our moral responsibility to take care of the environment and ecosystem. For sustenance in the universe, we have to depend on the ecosystem. So, instead of limiting ourselves to mechanical development, we have to work by cultivating intellect and conscience to create a habitable earth for future generations.”
Highlighting the global context of the climate crisis, he said temperatures are rising due to carbon emissions caused by excessive use of fossil fuels. Coastal low-lying areas face the risk of being inundated, he said, adding there is no alternative to greening and afforestation to overcome this global crisis.
Swapon recalled that Shaheed President Ziaur Rahman had taken far-sighted initiatives for environmental conservation and launched the tree plantation movement alongside ensuring food security in the country.
In continuation of that, the present government, under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, has adopted a mega plan to plant 250 million trees over the next five years, he said, adding that this year’s target has already been successfully achieved.
He strongly urged for extensive expansion of greening across the country with the participation of every family, educational institution, and social organization under the concept “One Child, One Tree."
At the same time, he called upon the agriculturalist community to play a leading role in making the social movement a success.
Agriculturist Dr Kamruzzaman Kaiser presided over the program while Nurul Islam Nayan MP, Shahidul Islam Bablu MP, Secretary of the Ministry of Agriculture Selim Khan, and leaders of the Krishibid Association spoke on the occasion.

item.title: Real Madrid snatch late win at Espanyol on Mourinho's return
item.description:
Jose Mourinho's second spell in charge of Real Madrid began with a last-gasp 2-1 victory at Espanyol in La Liga on Saturday, with substitute Carlos Espi pouncing in the 90th minute to grab the winner.
Jude Bellingham opened the scoring in Los Blancos' opening fixture of the season, and new signing Espi secured the points at the death after Alex Calatrava had levelled against Mourinho's star-studded team.
"I think that we deserved to win but that Espanyol didn't deserve to lose," Mourinho told reporters.
"They didn't have any players at the World Cup and have been working together for a long time, and you could see that."
Back in charge of Madrid 13 years after leaving, Portuguese veteran Mourinho must bring the dressing room under control after the chaos of last season, and end Spanish champions Barcelona's domestic dominance.
Mourinho started with superstars Kylian Mbappe, Vinicius Junior and Bellingham, as well as handing debuts to Bernardo Silva, Denzel Dumfries and Ibrahima Konate.
Bellingham had an excellent first season at Madrid after arriving from Borussia Dortmund but the subsequent two were disappointing, both for him and the club, who failed to win a major trophy in either.
Mourinho installed him in attacking midfield with licence to roam and the former Birmingham man was heavily involved before his goal as Madrid probed.
The England international netted the first of Mourinho's second era at the club, heading home Arda Guler's dangerous crossed free-kick.
Espanyol threatened midway through the first half as Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois beat away Clemens Riedel's drive and Roberto Fernandez hooked over shortly afterwards.
Madrid did not heed the warning and Espanyol levelled in the 30th minute, Calatrava slotting home Javi Hernandez's cut-back after a fine team move.
- Intense battle -
Espanyol stopper Marko Dmitrovic made a good save to stop Mbappe after he got in behind on the right of the area.
The French forward, La Liga's top scorer in both of his two seasons at the club, was not at his lethal best in front of goal.
On the left flank Vinicius had little impact, beyond winning a series of fouls from Espanyol players who were determined to shut him down by any means.
"Vini is not a saint, but what they do to im is too much, it started in the first minute, I think it's something systemic, it's done in a systemic way," said Mourinho.
"First I hack him, then you, then me, then you, if I get a yellow then you do it. I have a yellow so I go off, and someone comes on without a yellow... it's frustrating for him."
Mourinho sent on two more new arrivals in the form of record signing Yan Diomande and Marc Cucurella as Madrid sought a winner in the final 25 minutes.
Federico Valverde hit the outside of the post with a low effort from the edge of the box as Espanyol dug deep to deny Madrid clear chances.
However in the 90th minute Madrid found the goal they needed when former Levante striker Espi, the lowest profile of Los Blancos' summer purchases, capitalised on a loose ball in the box and fired home.
"We carried out our plan well and then let in that goal at the end," said Calatrava.
"That we conceded was a gut-punch, because we worked hard until the end."
Earlier, Sevilla won 3-1 at Athletic Bilbao and Valencia and Celta Vigo drew 0-0.
On Sunday champions Barcelona play their first game of the season at Elche, while Atletico Madrid host Villarreal.

item.description:
Health officials on Saturday said they recorded 702 fresh cases of dengue onslaughts in the past 24 hours.
"During the period, (of the 702) 115 patients were hospitalized in Barisal division, 107 in Chittagong division, 47 in Dhaka division, 88 in Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) and 123 in Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) areas, 114 in Khulna division, 38 in Mymensingh division, 54 in Rajshahi division and 15 in Rangpur division, a Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) statement said.
Since the start of the dengue onslaught in Bangladesh, this year witnessed so far 77 deaths, while the disease inflicted 28,090 people.
Last year, the mosquito-borne disease claimed 413 lives and inflicted 1,02,861 people in the country, while it claimed 575 lives and inflicted 1,01,214 people in 2024.

item.title: CDA to build tourist zone at Karnaphuli bank in Chittagong
item.description:
Chittagong Development Authority (CDA) is set to establish a three-kilometer tourist zone on the bank of the Karnaphuli River in Bakalia region of the port city.
This initiative will be implemented under a project named "Construction of Road on the bank of River Karnaphuli from Kalurghat bridge to Chaktai Khal (canal)."
CDA’s chief town planner Abu Issa Anshary informed BSS that a walkway will also be constructed over a five-kilometer area extending from Shah Amanat Bridge to Bolirhat. Additionally, a restaurant catering to tourists and a complete entertainment options for children will be built. The funds allocated for this project will be utilized to create various tourist attractions, he noted. Local resident Jabed Ahmed remarked: "The socio-economic conditions of this area will improve significantly if the tourism zone is established." He further stated that Chittagong and its neighboring upazilas possess numerous features that appeal to tourists, such as stunning sea views, mountains, mangrove forests, waterfalls, and lakes.
However, the potential of many tourist sites has largely gone unexploited due to the lack of interest from the government agencies.
Architect Shahinul Islam Khan, the former chief urban planner of the CDA, emphasized the necessity for authorities to maintain the cleanliness of the river. He stated that establishing an eco-friendly tourist center in this area would significantly transform the port city into a genuine tourist destination. Data from the CDA indicates that the project received approval during a meeting of the Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC) on April 25, 2017. The construction phase of the project commenced on June 2019 with the initiation of a sluice gate at the estuary of the Chaktai canal. Project Director Rajib Das stated: "Upon completion of the construction, this road will link the Dhaka-Chittagong and Chittagong-Cox’s Bazar highways via the City Bypass Loop Road and the Oxygen-Quaish Link Road, thereby alleviating traffic congestion within the city." He further explained that vehicles arriving from Kaptai, Rangunia, and Boalkhali upazilas will be able to bypass the city center using this road, facilitating access to the city’s airport, Patenga area, and southern Chittagong. Tourists from Chittagong city, as well as the northern and southern districts, will soon be able to enjoy the tourist zone. He additionally stated that 92% of the construction for this 9.5-kilometer-long road has been finalized. The remaining tasks are anticipated to be completed by December. Once the road is fully functional, it will offer numerous advantages, he added.
So, it will open up new opportunities for managing waterlogging in the city, safeguarding riverbanks, enhancing urban connectivity, establishing a modern water drainage system, and promoting the tourism industry.
CDA chairman engineer Belayet Hossain informed BSS that the project has been incorporated into the CDA Master Plan, with plans to establish a three-kilometer-long tourist zone. Efforts are underway to develop these areas through private or joint venture initiatives.
He mentioned that a walkway extending over three kilometers from Shah Amanat Bridge to Bolirhat will be constructed, along with a tourist center on both the sides of Marine Drive. A family-friendly restaurant featuring entertainment options for children will be established, he said. The CDA chairman noted that Bakalia is regarded as one of the less developed regions of Chittagong city.
Urban planners assert that the successful execution of this plan could significantly transform the area's landscape. They believe that the quality of life for local residents will also enhance following the project's completion. Despite Bakalia being a densely populated area, it lacks essential entertainment facilities.
So, this new tourist center is expected to provide opportunities for the residents of Bakalia, as well as the broader Chittagong city, to enjoy nature in close proximity, they remarked. Although Bakalia is a crowded locality, there are insufficient arrangements for the entertainment of its inhabitants. Thus, the new tourist destination will enable individuals not only from Bakalia but from the entire Chittagong city to engage with nature, he concluded.

item.title: Six Bangladeshi hotel fire victims repatriated from Kolkata
item.description:
The bodies of six Bangladeshis killed in a hotel fire in Kolkata on Wednesday have been repatriated to Bangladesh through the Bhomra and Benapole borders.
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs said in a press release on Saturday that the Bangladesh Deputy High Commission in Kolkata coordinated with local authorities and the victims’ families to complete the necessary formalities and facilitate the repatriation.
The body of SM Alimuzzaman of Satkhira was brought back through the Ghojadanga-Bhomra border on Saturday morning and handed over to his family.
The bodies of four members of a Kushtia family — Debashish Dutta, Afsana Sharmin, Shornoshish Dutta and Md Akram Ali — and Babu Ahmed of Aminbazar in Dhaka were repatriated through the Petrapole-Benapole border on Saturday afternoon.
The deputy high commission provided the families with necessary assistance throughout the process, including preservation, transportation and repatriation of the bodies.
The body of the seventh victim, Repti Sarkar of Satkhira, was cremated in Kolkata on Friday night at the family’s request. The deputy high commission also provided financial and other assistance for the cremation.
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs expressed deep condolences to the bereaved families of those killed in the fire.

item.title: Humaiun: No rush on PM’s India visit, national interest comes first
item.description:
Newly appointed State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir on Saturday said Prime Minister Tarique Rahman will visit India at an appropriate time following progress in discussions, with the country’s national interests being given priority.
He said the government wants to maintain a positive and effective relationship with India, but Bangladesh cannot move forward with relations with any country by compromising its national interests.
The state minister made the remarks while responding to queries from journalists after paying homage to the Liberation War martyrs at the National Memorial in Savar at noon.
Regarding relations with India, he said, “We want a positive relationship with India. Why wouldn’t we? They are our neighbours. We should have an effective relationship.”
However, Kobir said there will be no compromise on Bangladesh’s national interests. “Not only with India, but with no country can we do anything by compromising our national interests,” he said.
About extradition of deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, he said she went to India after fleeing Bangladesh following her involvement in the killing of 1,500 people during the July 2024 mass uprising, and that judicial proceedings in several cases against her have already reached conclusions, while many other cases remain pending.
The state minister said Bangladesh has an extradition treaty with India. “So, these are not new conditions or a new kind of engagement; these are ongoing issues,” he said.
He said bringing back Hasina and other alleged offenders who fled to India is linked to the expectations of the people of Bangladesh.
“There are more criminals who have fled to India. This is a natural demand of the people of Bangladesh and a matter of their sentiment. We want to engage with India by giving priority to this process,” Kobir said.
“We will engage with India. We want a positive relationship. But it has to be done by prioritising Bangladesh’s national interests,” he said, adding that there is no rush over the Prime Minister’s India visit.
“If we reach an agreement based on our national interests tomorrow, we can go [to India] next week, or the week after. There is no rush here,” the state minister said.
He said necessary preparations and discussions are required before a visit at the prime ministerial level.
“There are issues to discuss and preparations to make. A prime ministerial-level visit is not something that can just happen suddenly. This is not a game,” Kobir said.
He said the two sides need to establish the necessary preparations and groundwork before a meeting between the heads of government. “We are doing exactly that,” he said.
The state minister said Bangladesh is receiving indications of a positive attitude and goodwill from India, noting that it has also acknowledged the sentiments of the people of Bangladesh.
“You can see that statements are also coming from India on this issue. They have acknowledged that the sentiments of the people of Bangladesh have been hurt, particularly by Sheikh Hasina’s press conference on August 5 this year. They have taken note of the matter,” he said, describing this as a “good beginning.”
“Now let us see whether there is some progress in the remaining discussions. Based on the discussions and our national interests, we will certainly visit India when the time is appropriate,” Kobir said.

item.title: Swapon: Yellow journalism increasingly blurs media standards
item.description:
Former Information and Broadcasting Minister Zahir Uddin Swapon on Saturday said the distinction between yellow and responsible journalism is increasingly becoming blurred, posing a major challenge for the media industry.
“The gap between yellow and responsible journalism has become increasingly pronounced, while the line distinguishing the two is gradually disappearing,” he said.
Swapon made the remarks while inaugurating the annual District Correspondents’ Conference of United News of Bangladesh (UNB) 2026 at the Cosmos Centre in Malibagh.
Speaking about the changing media landscape, he said readership of print newspapers is declining as people are increasingly becoming device-oriented, while digital platforms have gained widespread dominance.
He said the key challenge for both traditional and digital media is to ensure that information remains objective as it moves from limited sources to a vast number of platforms.
Swapon urged responsible journalists to help curb yellow journalism and separate mainstream media from what he described as “parasitic media” and “digital junk”.
He also highlighted the need to distinguish investigative journalism from an intelligence-gathering mindset and urged the media to move from event-based reporting towards knowledge-based and comprehensive journalism.
He identified “objectivity versus instant sensation” as another major challenge in the digital era, warning that the rush to break news could undermine a media organization’s credibility.
“The credibility and credentials of a media organization are like glass. They can break or develop a crack in a single incident,” he said.
Swapon also called for stronger attention to journalists’ wages, job security and working conditions, stressing the importance of compliance with the Wage Board. He said media owners must ensure proper salary structures, job security, a safe working environment and gender equality.
He also called for clear editorial policies and an appropriate regulatory framework for the media industry.
Swapon said he hoped his successor, Barrister Andaleeve Rahman Partho, would maintain continuity in the sector. He also said he is likely to move as an adviser on media and related issues to the prime minister’s Office.
UNB Editor-in-Chief Enayetullah Khan welcomed the participants at the conference. Several senior journalists, media professionals and officials also spoke at the event.

item.title: Amir Khosru: Higher education must be linked to employment, entrepreneurship
item.description:
Finance and Planning Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury on Friday called for linking higher education with employment and entrepreneurship, urging authorities to consider priority sectors, employment prospects and entrepreneurial opportunities while establishing new universities and introducing new faculties and subjects.
“Higher education subjects and curricula must be determined in line with the country’s economic needs and labour market realities. The goal of higher education should not be limited to obtaining certificates; it should also prepare students for employment and entrepreneurship,” he said.
The minister was addressing the ‘Vice-Chancellors' Dialogue: Shaping the Future of Higher Education’, a two-day national policy dialogue organised under the Higher Education Acceleration and Transformation (HEAT) Project of the University Grants Commission (UGC) at BRAC CDM in Savar.
He also stressed the need for stronger university-industry collaboration, saying universities and industries in many countries maintain close links and Bangladesh should utilise the potential of such cooperation.
“Why can’t we develop industry-university interaction in Bangladesh? Around the world, universities and industries are seriously connected. We need to utilise this potential,” he said.
Amir Khosru said international and national rankings of higher education institutions have an impact not only on employment opportunities and global recognition but also on the overall image of a country.
He urged universities to identify the reasons behind the weak university-industry linkage and the mismatch between education and labour market requirements.
“Why can’t we change our education system in relation to the job market?” he asked, stressing the need to establish a stronger relationship between education and employment.
The minister also underscored the importance of research as a fundamental component of higher education and called for linking research with industry.
“Research is fundamental for education. We need to determine our priorities in research and explore how we can connect research with industry,” he said.
He urged universities to conduct research to address real-life problems faced by industries and businesses and called upon the private sector to finance university research and commercially utilise research findings.
“Research should not remain confined to publications; it must contribute to national development and people’s welfare,” he said.
Questioning the academic structure of newly established universities, Amir Khosru said their faculties and academic programmes should be selected based on specific educational, regional and employment needs.
“I do not know under what consideration these faculties have been selected. I don’t see the reason,” he said. He said establishing new universities was a positive development, but their academic programmes should be designed to address the needs of the regions where they are located.
“What target are we trying to fulfil through these universities? Do people in those areas have proper opportunities to enter the job market?” he asked.
He said newly established universities have an advantage as they could be designed from the beginning to address existing challenges in higher education.
The minister said he would request the UGC to formulate appropriate guidelines on the faculties and subjects to be introduced at newly established universities, taking into account regional needs, priority sectors and employment opportunities.

item.title: Drive begins to revive navigability of Old Buriganga
item.description:
A massive cleanliness drive began on Friday at the Durani canal and adjacent areas to revive the navigability of the Old Buriganga channel, a 7-kilometre historical waterway near Kamrangirchar and Rasulpur in Dhaka.
The Dhaka district administration, along with volunteer-based youth organization "BD Clean", jointly launched the drive.
The drive began following the Prime Minister’s directive to State Minister for Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives, Mir Shahe Alam, to revive the channel after removing waste dumps.
In line with the directive, initiatives have been taken for re-excavation, eviction drives and dredging projects to revive the blocked waterway, restore navigability and build modern civic walkways.
Before starting the drive, the LGRD state minister administered an oath to stakeholders, including members of BD Clean.
Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) Administrator M Abdus Salam, Hamidur Rahman, MP of Dhaka-7, and Dhaka Deputy Commissioner Farida Khanam were also present.
A cleanliness drive is launched at the Durani canal and adjacent areas to revive the navigability of the Old Buriganga channel in Dhaka on Friday, August 21, 2026. Photo: BSS
Approximately 1,000 feet of the 3.2-km-long Old Buriganga channel, the oldest water channel in Old Dhaka, located around the Durani Bridge area, as well as different parts of the channel, have become waste-dumping sites due to land encroachment.
The obstruction of water flow, along with bad smells, mosquito menace and waterlogging, has caused immense suffering to local residents.
According to experts, the normal water flow of the Old Buriganga channel was hampered following the construction of the Dhaka flood-control embankment, widely known as the Beribadh, in the early 1990s to protect the western and northern parts of the city from seasonal river floods.
Under the circumstances, the government has taken a fresh initiative to make the channel an eco-friendly and public-friendly water body.
Waste disposal inside the channel and its adjacent areas has begun, while an awareness programme is also being conducted among local people, urging them not to dump waste at the waterway.
After completion of the cleanliness drive, initiatives will be taken to restore the navigability of the channel, said DSCC sources, adding that beautification will be carried out on both sides of the channel and civic walkways will also be constructed for the recreation of local residents.
Inaugurating the cleanliness drive, the state minister said: “It is imperative to keep canals and rivers free from waste to protect the environment and public health. The joint initiative of the Dhaka district administration and BD Clean is praiseworthy.”
“We hope that the programme will be successfully completed and local people will benefit from it,” he added.
Alongside the cleanliness drive, the Dhaka district administration will maintain surveillance to ensure that the channel is not encroached upon or polluted again.

item.title: Three top criminals arrested in Mohammadpur
item.description:
Rapid Action Battalion (RAB-2) has arrested three alleged criminals, including a teen gang member, in separate raids in the capital’s Mohammadpur area.
The arrestees are Mohammad Selim Ashrafi alias Chua Selim, a top drug dealer and alleged criminal from Geneva Camp; Joy, second-in-command of the Mahi teen gang; and Mohammad Ratan alias Boma Ratan, a listed criminal.
RAB-2 Commander Additional DIG Naimul Hasan disclosed the information at a press briefing at the battalion’s Basila office on Friday.
He said Chua Selim, accused in 36 cases and wanted in murder and drug-related cases, was arrested from Geneva Camp with a foreign-made pistol, two rounds of ammunition and 110 grams of heroin.
According to RAB, Chua Selim had long been involved in drug trafficking, mugging, murder, clashes and other criminal activities in and around Geneva Camp. He was previously arrested from Dhanmondi on January 8 last year.
On the same day, RAB-2 arrested Joy from Chand Udyan. He is accused in 10 cases involving robbery, mugging and drug-related offences.
RAB said Joy and other members of the Mahi gang had long been involved in mugging, extortion and assaults in Dhaka Udyan, Chand Udyan and Nabinagar, creating fear among residents. Local businesspeople, tenants and construction workers were allegedly regular targets of extortion.
Joy was also arrested by law enforcement agencies from Mohammadpur on April 24 this year.
In a separate operation, RAB-2 arrested listed criminal Mohammad Ratan alias Boma Ratan from Bijli Mohalla in Mohammadpur.
Ratan is accused in 20 cases involving robbery, dacoity, mugging and arms offences, RAB said.
According to the elite force, Boma Ratan had long led an armed gang involved in robbery, mugging and other criminal activities in Gaznabi Road, Basila and Geneva Camp.
He was previously detained with a sharp weapon from Gaznabi Road on February 19, 2022.

item.title: Bangabhaban bids farewell to Acting President Hafiz Uddin
item.description:
Bangabhaban on Thursday bade a grand farewell to Acting President Hafiz Uddin Ahmad Bir Bikram through a state ceremony. A smartly turned-out contingent of President Guard Regiment (PGR) of the army extended him a guard of honour while a band group comprising military, navy, and air force played the farewell tune at 11.30 am.
Another group of the horse-mounted troops of Bangladesh Police escorted him forward as part of the farewell ceremony.
The acting president signed the Bangbhaban visitors’ book and exchanged greetings with Bangabhaban officials and employees.
On July 25, Speaker of Parliament Hafiz Uddin Ahmad Bir Bikram assumed the responsibilities of the acting President in accordance with the Constitution following the resignation of former president Mohammed Shahabuddin.

item.title: Dengue: Two more die as 671 cases recorded in 24 hours
item.description:
Health officials on Wednesday said they recorded 671 fresh cases of dengue onslaughts killing at least two persons in the past 24 hours.
"During the period, (of the 671) 70 patients were hospitalized in Barisal division, 83 in Chittagong division, 119 in Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) and 130 in Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) areas, 133 in Khulna division, 35 in Mymensingh division, 92 in Rajshahi division and six in Rangpur division and three in Sylhet division, a Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) statement said.
Since the start of the dengue onslaughts Bangladesh this year witnessed so far 76 deaths while the disease inflicted 26,272.
The dengue last year claimed 413 lives and inflicted 1,02,861 people in the country.
Besides, the dengue claimed 575 lives and inflicted 1,01,214 people in 2024.

item.title: Private clinics mushroom across Naogaon, raising regulatory concerns
item.description:
Private hospitals, clinics and diagnostic centres have mushroomed across Naogaon’s 11 upazilas, raising concerns over facilities allegedly operating without proper documents and approvals.
Many of these establishments have reportedly been operating for years despite lacking the required paperwork, while authorities often appear to step up enforcement only after serious incidents, including patient deaths allegedly linked to medical negligence.
Once administrative drives subside, however, some of the facilities reportedly resume operations.
Several private establishments also lack the infrastructure and environment required to provide proper medical care, raising concerns about patient safety.
The proliferation of private facilities around government upazila health complexes has added to the problem. Patients and locals allege that brokers representing private hospitals, clinics and diagnostic centres remain stationed around government hospitals to divert patients to private facilities.
There are also allegations that some doctors working at government health complexes have arrangements with private hospitals, clinics and diagnostic centres.
Patients from remote areas seeking treatment at government facilities are sometimes allegedly pushed into undergoing unnecessary diagnostic tests, even when they seek treatment for common ailments.
Patients have also complained about the behaviour of some government doctors, shortages of medicines and the irregular availability of physicians. They said these problems have contributed to growing dissatisfaction with government healthcare services.
By contrast, private facilities are often perceived as offering more attentive care and better treatment to patients in exchange for payment, encouraging more people to seek treatment there.
According to the Naogaon Civil Surgeon’s Office, the district has 115 registered private hospitals and clinics across its 11 upazilas. Naogaon Sadar has the highest number, with 43.
An application has recently been submitted to establish a facility named Science Lab and Hospital in Naogaon Sadar.
Meanwhile, Ekta Clinic at Saraigachhi intersection in Porsha and Porsha Islami Lab and Hospital have been ordered to shut down, according to the Civil Surgeon’s Office.
Civil Surgeon Dr Md Aminul Islam said the health department was working to bring greater transparency to the district’s healthcare sector.
“Whenever we receive allegations or find irregularities involving private hospitals, clinics or diagnostic centres, we conduct drives and take immediate action,” he said.
He said the district’s healthcare services had improved significantly compared with the past.
The health department would continue its efforts to eliminate irregularities, the civil surgeon said, urging people with specific complaints to submit them in writing so authorities could investigate and take appropriate action.
